stocks.headline: Down 14.0% Friday to 125.53, a new 52-week low, and now 136.16 premarket (+8.5%) after the Treasury Secretary refused to rule out Huang returning as CEO.
stocks.why: The business has not broken. Sales are up 106%, the operating margin is 65%, and the stock trades at 8x next year's profit, its cheapest in 5 years. It is down 19.3% since a beat because the CEO left, TSMC and Samsung halted some chip shipments to China, and a state probe is looking into chips being diverted to China. Today's jump is a bet on who will lead the company, not on any new business facts. Whatever Nvidia does today will carry TSM, AVGO, ARM, MU, SMCI and CRWV with it.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. The stock is very cheap for this growth, but nobody knows who runs the company or how much China revenue is at risk, and the price has not stopped falling.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A firm answer on leadership, or clear limits on the China shipment halt and the probes, would make it a Buy at these prices.
stocks.action: Don't buy the +8.5% gap. Buy a small starter only if it trades back above 143.73 (Friday's high), which would show buyers in control.

levels.means: above = Friday's selling is undone and a starter is justified; below = the bounce is still unproven
above = the gap is holding; below = the bounce has failed
above = the 52-week low holds; below = new lows and no floor in sight

stocks.if_then: If it falls back below 125.53, then stay out all day and expect the 124.5 low to be tested.

stocks.headline: Fell 8.5% Friday to 101.19, just above its 52-week low of 100.25, and is 105.99 premarket (+4.7%). The stock is down 59.3% from its high.
stocks.why: The selling is about fear over AI spending: Microsoft is using fewer outside AI cloud providers and Google and Microsoft held back on capex. Oracle's own numbers keep getting better. Sales are up 30% and speeding up, it has beaten forecasts 4 quarters running, the contracted backlog is $664.0B, and it trades at 9x next year's profit. The real risk is that the customers behind that backlog cut back, and the Dec 14 report (typical move 11%, profit expected down 16%) is where that shows. Weak results from HPE today or DELL tomorrow would hit it too.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view (Buy now). Growth is speeding up, the backlog is huge and the price is its cheapest in 5 years, so the AI-spending scare looks priced in.

stocks.what_would_change_it: If the Dec 14 report shows the backlog shrinking or customers pushing out contracts, the stance drops to Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy the open. Buy a first third only on a dip to 101.19 that holds above 100.25, and leave room to add after Dec 14.

levels.means: above = the bounce is real and you can wait for a dip; below = a pullback toward 101.19 is likely
at or below = the buy zone for the first piece
above = the 52-week low holds; below = stop buying and wait for the report

stocks.if_then: If it breaks below 100.25, then stop buying and hold off until the Dec 14 report.

stocks.headline: Fell 9.2% Friday to 21.65, near its 20-day low of 21.47, and is 22.97 premarket (+6.1%) after a report that Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are raising AI server prices on deals already signed.
stocks.why: Raising prices after a deal is signed means the server makers' own costs are rising, mainly memory, which fits MU's 345% sales growth. Supermicro makes only $12 of gross profit per $100 of sales, so passing costs on protects its thin profit. The danger is that buyers balk, delay or cancel orders, and that would land on SMCI, DELL and HPE together. HPE's results today and Dell's tomorrow are the first test of whether buyers will pay.

long_term.reason: It trades at 3x next year's profit and sales are up 298%, but margins are wafer-thin, analysts rate it hold, and the house swing view is Avoid until the trend turns.

stocks.what_would_change_it: HPE and Dell reporting that customers accepted the higher prices without cutting orders would make it a buy.
stocks.action: Don't buy before HPE and Dell report. Sell into the +6.1% gap if you hold it as a trade.

levels.means: above = Friday's high is taken back and the sellers are tiring; below = the downtrend holds
above = the 20-day low holds; below = new lows toward 19.48

stocks.if_then: If HPE says customers are pushing back on prices, then stay out through Dell's report tomorrow.
